scenario: [LTIM.2.5.2] edge-once RE-ARM after retract — a now()-gated rule fires once on the false->true edge (edge-once, [LTIM.2.5.1]), stays suppressed on later ticks while the matched fact lives, and then RE-ARMS once that fact retracts and a fresh one is asserted. Companion to LTIM.2.5 (which pins the single-fact suppression): this pins the full lifecycle across a retract. The persistent one-shot keys on the matched fact's fact_id and is cleared when that fact leaves WM; the re-asserted fact carries a fresh monotonic id absent from the one-shot, so it re-arms. Pin: mature+pump (fire 1), pump (suppressed), retract, re-assert, pump (fire 2 — re-armed), pump (suppressed). Exactly two fires; the naive fire-every-tick impl would fire four+ times and fail this exact match.
rules_ds:
import calendar

schema Sensor scope logical:
    entity_id: String key

rule after_5_s:
    Sensor where now() > calendar.time(1970, 1, 1, 0, 0, 5)
->
    log info "time passed"
